tables.name: Jobs
tables.description:
## Purpose
Transform validated commercial and location context into executable operational work records.

## Key data
- Scheduling context
- Assignment context
- Execution context
- Completion outputs
- Linked operational dependencies

## Relationship
- One quote → many jobs
- One location → many jobs
- One job → many tasks
- One job → many tickets
- One job → many inventory links

## Scale
Can contain large volumes of operational records across installations, maintenance, transit, and support-related activities.

## Lifecycle
- Created once an operational need is confirmed
- Moves through explicit operational statuses and execution stages
- Closed when execution evidence and downstream sync requirements are completed

## Role in system (Operational orchestration layer)
- Acts as the central execution object for operational work
- Represents the main orchestration layer between commercial scope and field execution

## Data consolidation scope

### Planning
- Scheduled dates
- Assigned partners
- Operational readiness

### Execution
- Installation work
- Delivery and collection
- Survey and rework
- Maintenance-linked work

### Dependencies
- BOM context
- Quote context
- Location context
- Inventory context

### Outputs
- Installation images
- Support images
- Delivery notes
- Job reports
- Sign-off artifacts

### Operational follow-through
- Linked tasks
- Linked tickets
- Linked maintenance records

## Data flow model
- Operational scope originates from:
  - Quotes
  - BOM
  - Location context
- Execution data is created and managed in:
  - Jobs
- Completion data is synced and linked onward into:
  - Inventory
  - Locations
  - Documents and downstream reporting layers

## System role
Single point of control for:
- Operational execution
- Assignment and scheduling
- Completion capture
- Downstream sync of field outcomes

tables.name: Tasks
tables.description:
## Purpose
Decompose jobs into assignable execution units for operational follow-through.

## Key data
- Linked parent job
- Task category
- Summary and description
- Subtasks
- Due date
- Assigned collaborators
- Attachments and notes

## Relationship
- One job → many tasks
- One task → one parent job

## Scale
Can contain multiple execution units per job across several operational phases.

## Lifecycle
- Created after or during job preparation
- Moves through explicit work states from backlog to closure or archival
- Completion can be tracked at both task and subtask level

## Role in system (Execution decomposition layer)
- Acts as the granular execution layer beneath Jobs
- Represents the work breakdown structure for operational delivery

## Data consolidation scope

### Execution phases
- Pre-installation
- Rollout
- CMS
- Post-installation
- Support
- Music
- Innovation

### Work tracking
- Status progression
- Due dates
- Ownership
- Attachments
- Notes

### Completion tracking
- Task-level completion
- Subtask-level completion
- Category-based progress contribution to parent job

## Data flow model
- Operational context originates from:
  - Jobs
- Granular execution data is managed in:
  - Tasks
- Completion data is rolled back into Jobs
- Segment-based progress is used to monitor execution readiness and operational follow-through

## System role
Single point of detail for:
- Granular operational execution
- Work assignment
- Progress tracking
- Phase-level completion measurement

tables.name: Quotes
tables.description:
## Purpose
Convert commercial demand into operationally usable scope for downstream planning and execution.

## Key data
- Commercial scope
- Customer-linked context
- Operational normalization inputs
- Downstream planning dependencies

## Relationship
- One quote → many jobs
- One quote → one or more BOM-linked execution structures

## Scale
Can contain multiple commercial records that expand into multiple downstream operational objects.

## Lifecycle
- Created as upstream commercial intake
- Enriched and normalized before downstream execution begins
- Consumed by downstream planning and operational creation flows

## Role in system (Commercial intake and normalization layer)
- Acts as the entry point between commercial demand and operations
- Represents the upstream scope-definition layer for execution planning

## Data consolidation scope

### Commercial context
- Customer demand
- Commercial scope
- Related commercial records

### Operational normalization
- Data required for downstream planning
- Execution dependencies
- Scope interpretation for jobs and BOM

### Downstream impact
- Job creation
- BOM creation
- Operational execution quality

## Data flow model
- Commercial demand originates in:
  - Upstream commercial source context
- Scope is normalized in:
  - Quotes
- Operational structures are created and linked onward into:
  - Jobs
  - BOM
  - Related downstream operational records

## System role
Single point of origin for:
- Commercial-to-operational translation
- Scope normalization
- Downstream planning integrity
- Execution readiness upstream

tables.name: BOM
tables.description:
## BOM
- **Purpose:**  
  Define the complete resource scope derived from a normalized quote and use it to structure execution planning in Jobs.  

- **Key data:**  
  - Link to quote  
  - Linked BOM resources  
  - Linked jobs  
  - Resource quantities  
  - Subscription context  
  - Validation and planning fields  

- **Relationship:**  
  - One quote → one or more BOMs  
  - One BOM → many BOM resources  
  - One BOM → many jobs  

- **Scale:**  
  Typically one per normalized quote, but can expand if scope is split operationally.  

- **Lifecycle:**  
  - Created after quote normalization  
  - Expanded through BOM resources  
  - Used for job creation and execution planning  
  - Retained as reference for validation and reporting  

- **Role in system (Commercial-to-operational bridge):**  
  Converts normalized quote scope into a structured execution-ready resource definition.

tables.name: BOM resources
tables.description:
## BOM Resources
- **Purpose:**  
  Represent the granular resource lines within a BOM so each quoted SKU becomes a deployable operational unit with quantity, inventory, and subscription linkage.  

- **Key data:**  
  - Resource  
  - Quantity  
  - BOM link  
  - Subscription contract linkage  
  - Inventory allocation fields  
  - Job planning distribution fields  

- **Relationship:**  
  - Many BOM resources → one BOM  
  - One resource → many BOM resources  
  - One BOM resource → one or more job allocations  

- **Scale:**  
  One record per resource line inside a BOM; scales with quote complexity.  

- **Lifecycle:**  
  - Created from normalized quote scope  
  - Used to earmark inventory and structure subscriptions  
  - Consumed during execution planning and installation  
  - Retained for audit and operational traceability  

- **Role in system (Execution granularity layer):**  
  Acts as the atomic layer between commercial scope and deployable execution components.

tables.name: Resources
tables.description:
## Purpose
Store synced resource master data used in Jobs for quote normalization, BOM construction, and operational planning.

## Key data
- Resource identity
- Service and category classification
- Brand and model
- SKU and imagery
- Inventory summary metrics

## Relationship
- One resource → many quote line mappings
- One resource → many BOM resource lines
- One resource → many inventory records in downstream inventory structures

## Scale
Can contain the full product and service catalog needed for operational planning across hardware, software, and service items.

## Lifecycle
- Originates in the Inventory base as master resource data
- Synced into Jobs for commercial-to-operational interpretation
- Used repeatedly across quote, BOM, and job preparation workflows

## Role in system (Synced resource master layer)
- Acts as the canonical product and service reference for operational planning in Jobs
- Represents the master SKU catalog used to interpret quoted scope and build BOMs

## Data consolidation scope

### Master resource identity
- Name
- SKU
- Brand and model
- Category and service tags

### Media and presentation
- Images
- Quote-facing formatted specs

### Inventory summary context
- Available, installed, in production, spare, defect, and other inventory rollups

## Data flow model
- Canonical resource data originates in:
  - Inventory base
- Synced resource master data is made available in:
  - Jobs → Resources
- Downstream consumers use this data through:
  - Quote line interpretation
  - BOM creation
  - Resource planning
  - Inventory-aware execution preparation

## System role
Single point of synced reference for:
- Resource master data
- SKU interpretation
- BOM input catalog
- Planning-ready product and service definitions"

tables.name: FS - Partners
tables.description:
## Purpose
Store external field service partner organizations used for job execution support, workforce grouping, and partner-level coordination.

## Key data
- Partner identity
- Country linkage and country code
- Contact details
- Linked workers
- Linked jobs
- Status and notes

## Relationship
- One partner → many workers
- One partner → many jobs
- Many partners → one or more countries

## Scale
Can contain multiple external partner organizations across operational regions and service footprints.

## Lifecycle
- Created when a field service partner is onboarded
- Maintained over time with contact, status, and workforce updates
- Used for assignment, coordination, and partner governance

## Role in system (External partner coordination layer)
- Acts as the partner-level operational directory for outsourced or external field execution
- Represents the organizational layer above FS - Workers

## Data consolidation scope

### Partner identity
- Partner name
- Computed display name
- Record identifier

### Contact context
- Contact name
- Phone number
- Email address

### Geographic scope
- Country linkage
- Country code

### Operational linkage
- Workers
- Jobs
- Status
- Notes

## Data flow model
- External partner data is managed in:
  - FS - Partners
- Workforce detail is linked through:
  - FS - Workers
- Operational usage flows into:
  - Job assignments
  - Partner coordination
  - Regional field execution oversight

## System role
Single point of record for:
- External service partner organizations
- Partner workforce grouping
- Partner-linked operational coordination

tables.name: FS - Workers
tables.description:
## Purpose
Store external field service worker records used for assignment, compliance, and partner workforce tracking.

## Key data
- Worker identity
- Nationality and country code
- Permit details
- Installation partner linkage
- Status and personnel notes

## Relationship
- Many workers → one installation partner
- One partner → many workers

## Scale
Can contain multiple workers per field service partner across different countries or partner organizations.

## Lifecycle
- Created when external workforce records are registered
- Maintained over time with permit, status, and identity updates
- Used for assignment and operational eligibility checks

## Role in system (External workforce layer)
- Acts as the worker-level personnel register for partner-managed field operations
- Represents the assignable individual workforce beneath FS - Partners

## Data consolidation scope

### Personnel identity
- Name
- Internal worker ID
- Identification number
- Date of birth

### Legal and compliance data
- Nationality
- Country code
- Permit number
- Permit expiration

### Operational linkage
- Installation partner
- Worker status
- Notes

## Data flow model
- External workforce data is managed in:
  - FS - Workers
- Partner linkage is maintained through:
  - FS - Partners
- Operational use flows into:
  - Assignment and partner oversight
  - Compliance review
  - Field service workforce management

## System role
Single point of record for:
- External field workers
- Workforce compliance tracking
- Partner-linked personnel availability"

tables.name: Job locations
tables.description:
## Purpose
Store the synced location master data used by the Jobs base as the operational site reference layer.

## Key data
- Customer-linked location identity
- Address and contact details
- Geographic attributes
- Opening and content hours
- Location-specific operational metadata

## Relationship
- One customer → many locations
- One location → many jobs
- One location → many inventory and maintenance associations through operational layers

## Scale
Can contain large numbers of customer sites used repeatedly across operational workflows.

## Lifecycle
- Originates in the Locations base as master data
- Synced bidirectionally into Jobs for operational use
- Extended in Jobs through contextual projection tables such as Job locations

## Role in system (Synced master location layer)
- Acts as the location reference layer for operational planning and execution in Jobs
- Represents the canonical site context used by jobs, tickets, maintenance, and deployment workflows

## Data consolidation scope

### Site identity
- Location code and name
- Customer and brand linkage
- Address and regional attributes

### Contact and timing context
- Contact details
- Opening hours
- Content hours

### Operational attributes
- Connectivity
- Site type
- Installation-related metadata
- Floor plans and images

## Data flow model
- Canonical location data originates in:
  - Locations base
- Synced location master data is made available in:
  - Jobs → Locations
- Downstream operational layers consume this data through:
  - Jobs
  - Job locations
  - Maintenance structures
  - Inventory associations

## System role
Single point of synced reference for:
- Operational site master data
- Customer-linked location context
- Planning and execution site details"

tables.name: Jobs - Schedule log
tables.description:
## Purpose
Store a historical audit trail of scheduling changes made to Jobs records.

## Key data
- Linked job
- Scheduled date snapshot
- Log creation timestamp

## Relationship
- One job → many schedule log entries
- One log entry → one parent job

## Scale
Can accumulate multiple records per job whenever scheduling changes occur.

## Lifecycle
- Created automatically when a job scheduling event is logged
- Retained as historical evidence of schedule changes
- Used for audit and timing analysis rather than current planning

## Role in system (Scheduling audit layer)
- Acts as the historical event log for job scheduling changes
- Represents temporal change tracking rather than active scheduling state

## Data consolidation scope

### Scheduling history
- Scheduled date at the time of logging
- Chronology of rescheduling events

### Audit context
- Parent job reference
- Creation timestamp of each log entry

## Data flow model
- Current planning state originates in:
  - Jobs
- Schedule change history is captured in:
  - Jobs - Schedule log
- Historical data can be used for:
  - Audit review
  - Reschedule pattern analysis
  - Lead-time and volatility tracking

## System role
Single point of record for:
- Job schedule change history
- Scheduling audit evidence
- Reschedule chronology"

tables.name: HS - Quotes - LI
tables.description:
## Purpose
Store the synced line-item detail of accepted HubSpot quotes so each quoted SKU, quantity, and billing parameter can be consumed downstream in Jobs.

## Key data
- Parent HubSpot quote link
- SKU and normalized SKU
- Quantity and pricing fields
- Billing cadence and duration fields
- Financial line metrics such as tax, discount, margin, and net amount

## Relationship
- Many line items → one HS - Quotes record
- One accepted HubSpot quote → many line items

## Scale
Can contain multiple line items per accepted quote, depending on commercial scope and product mix.

## Lifecycle
- Created when an accepted HubSpot quote is hydrated into Airtable
- Synced into Jobs together with the quote header
- Consumed downstream for quote normalization, BOM creation, and operational planning

## Role in system (Commercial line-detail intake layer)
- Acts as the granular commercial payload beneath HS - Quotes
- Represents the line-level bridge between HubSpot quote content and downstream operational structures

## Data consolidation scope

### Commercial detail
- SKU-level quoted items
- Quantity and unit pricing
- Term totals and billing data

### Subscription structure
- Billing frequency
- Number of payments
- Duration and normalized duration
- Billing start date

### Financial detail
- Discounts
- Tax
- Margin
- Net amount
- COGS

## Data flow model
- Commercial quote content originates in:
  - HubSpot accepted quotes
- Line-item detail is hydrated into:
  - Quote - Line Items
- Downstream systems consume this detail for:
  - Quote normalization
  - BOM creation
  - Subscription interpretation
  - Operational resource planning

## System role
Single point of detail for:
- Accepted HubSpot quote line items
- SKU-level commercial scope
- Billing and duration interpretation
- Downstream operational decomposition"
